report.headline: Below-average NBA usage translates to a projected 22.1% usage rate in the EuroLeague, comfortably above league average, though the true shooting projection carries no signal at all

projection.text: The model projects a 22.1% usage rate in the EuroLeague, up from a 15.3% usage rate in the NBA and above the EuroLeague's 20.6% minutes-weighted average, with an 80% interval of 17.6% to 26.5% — a span of roughly two standard deviations of league usage (4.4%), so it can place the subject in the upper-middle of the usage distribution but not pin an exact number.

risks.text: The subject's NBA usage rate of 15.3% stood 0.97 standard deviations below the league average, a below-average role for a player making this particular transition, whose cohort typically sat only 0.31 standard deviations below their own league on entry.

The 80% prediction interval for usage rate spans 17.6% to 26.5%, roughly two full standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution (4.4%), meaning the model can rank this player relative to peers but cannot price an individual outcome precisely.

The true shooting projection of 63.6% is not trustworthy: the model's error (4.7%) is identical to the error of just guessing the league mean (4.7%), so this metric carries no usable information here.

The true shooting slope for this transition is only 0.536, meaning a little over half of a player's standing above their league average tends to carry over, well below the near-full carryover (0.986) seen for usage rate.

strengths.text: The subject carried a well above-average NBA true shooting mark of 64.7%, standing +1.93 standard deviations above the league that season, reflecting elite efficiency for the role played.
The usage projection model beats the trivial league-mean baseline (3.3% error vs 4.3%), giving some confidence to the direction and rough magnitude of the projected usage increase.

The projected 22.1% usage rate sits above both the EuroLeague average of 20.6% and the naive z-preservation baseline of 16.3%, consistent with the historical pattern that usage often expands on this move despite a below-average NBA role.

uncertainty.text: For true shooting, the model's out-of-fold error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the EuroLeague average (also 4.7%), so the 63.6% true shooting projection should not be treated as informative despite its narrow-looking central value.
